message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know or dive deeper into any part that interests you.

| # | Task | What You’ll Need | Tips |
|---|------|------------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | List of components (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling, OS) | Use PCPartPicker to check compatibility and price. |
| 2 | **Gather Tools** | Phillips screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap (optional), cable ties, thermal paste (if not pre‑applied) | Keep the workspace clean and static‑free. |
| 3 | **Prepare the Case** | Open the side panel, remove any pre‑installed parts | Label screws for later reassembly. |
| 4 | **Install the CPU** | CPU, motherboard, CPU cooler | Align the notch, gently place, secure the lever. |
| 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste** | If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste | Small pea‑size amount in the center. |
| 6 | **Mount the CPU Cooler** | Cooler, mounting bracket, screws | Follow cooler’s manual; ensure even pressure. |
| 7 | **Insert RAM** | RAM sticks, motherboard | Click until the latches lock. |
| 8 | **Install the M.2 SSD (if applicable)** | M.2 SSD, screw | Slide at 30° angle, then lock. |
| 9 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Motherboard, standoffs, screws | Align with case holes, tighten evenly. |
|10 | **Install the Power Supply** | PSU, screws | Secure to the back of the case, connect the 24‑pin and 8‑pin power cables. |
|11 | **Install Storage Drives** | 2.5″ SSD/HDD, 3.5″ HDD, drive bays, screws | Mount in the appropriate bay, connect SATA + power. |
|12 | **Install the Graphics Card** | GPU, PCI‑e slot, screws | Insert firmly, secure to the case. |
|13 | **Connect All Cables** | SATA data, SATA power, USB headers, front panel connectors, fan headers | Refer to motherboard manual for exact pins. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Cable ties, Velcro straps | Route cables behind the motherboard tray, keep airflow clear. |
|15 | **Final Check** | Verify all connections, no loose screws | Double‑check power cables and data cables. |
|16 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse | First boot → BIOS → set boot order, enable XMP for RAM. |
|17 | **Install Operating System** | USB flash drive with OS installer | Boot from USB, follow installation wizard. |
|18 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | GPU drivers, chipset drivers, Windows updates | Use manufacturer sites or Windows Update. |
|19 | **Test & Benchmark** | Stress test software (Prime95, FurMark), benchmark tools (Cinebench, 3DMark) | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits. |
|20 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Regular dust cleaning, monitor temperatures | Keep the case open for airflow, update drivers. |

---

#### Detailed Tips & Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **CPU not seated properly** | Re‑open the CPU socket, align the triangle, gently lower the lever. |
| **RAM not recognized** | Try swapping slots, ensure both sticks are fully inserted. |
| **GPU not detected** | Check that the PCI‑e slot is unlocked, reseat the card, ensure the power connector is attached. |
| **No display** | Verify monitor cable is connected to the GPU, not the motherboard. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure the cooler is properly mounted, fans are spinning, and airflow is unobstructed. |
| **Static damage** | Ground yourself before touching components, use an anti‑static mat. |

---

#### Quick Component Checklist

| Category | Example Choices |
|----------|-----------------|
| **CPU** | Intel i5‑13600K, AMD Ryzen 5 7600X |
| **Motherboard** | Z690 / B660 (Intel), X670 / B650 (AMD) |
| **RAM** | 16 GB DDR5‑6000 (2×8 GB) |
| **GPU** | RTX 3060 Ti, Radeon RX 6700 XT |
| **Storage** | 1 TB NVMe SSD (PCI‑e 4.0) |
| **PSU** | 650 W 80+ Gold |
| **Case** | Mid‑tower ATX, good airflow |
| **Cooling** | 120 mm AIO liquid cooler or high‑performance air cooler |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build & compare parts, check compatibility.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, cooler, and PSU manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for more detailed help. Happy building!
